title: The 5 Hidden Dojos For Better Coding
subtitle: Popular sites give you problems. These build how you think.
intro: Tutorials stopped working and you ask: which site will actually make me better? Your save has five hidden answers that build depth, not dopamine.
takeaway: Get better by training how you think, not just solving more problems.

sections.heading: Analogy: Your coding gym
sections.body:
Think of learning coding like training at a gym. One machine builds one muscle.

VisuAlgo is the mirror that shows your form for algorithms, so you see how they move. Project Euler is heavy math weights for problem decomposition, which means breaking a big puzzle into small steps.

This sets up why you need different gyms for different skills.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? To build real instincts
sections.body:
Popular platforms give you lots of problems. These five exist to build engineering instincts.

Exercism gives you human feedback to learn clean code, which means code that is easy to read and change. Refactoring Guru teaches design patterns, which are reusable solutions to common problems.

For example, you can practice one Codewars kata, which is a small repeated exercise, until you handle every edge-case, which is an unusual input that breaks sloppy code.

But more practice can still go wrong, as the next part shows.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? Practice without clarity
sections.body:
If you chase the viral, easy-dopamine feeling, you feel productive instantly but don't improve how you think.

What fails first if you just grind kata after kata with no feedback? You memorize tricks but can't read and refactor real code.

To avoid that, use the right site for the right weakness: VisuAlgo for intuition, Exercism for clarity, Refactoring Guru for design.

steps.narration: You feel tutorials no longer help you grow.
Use VisuAlgo to visualize how an algorithm actually runs.
Use Project Euler to practice breaking math problems into steps.
Use Codewars katas to train on tricky edge-cases.
Use Exercism and Refactoring Guru to make code clean and well-designed.
